Subject: Hosted API pricing: sustained QPS ceiling & monthly token envelope — follow-up

Hi Rohan / Ava — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can lock down a hosted pricing proposal: 

1) Monthly token envelope: you mentioned the proof-of-concept plus pilot could land in the ~60M-120M token/month band. Can you confirm what the expected steady-state run rate is after pilot (best guess)? Please indicate a single most-likely number if useful.

2) Peak / sustained QPS: we need two numbers —
  - expected 99th-percentile peak TPS during the busiest windows
  - a sustained QPS ceiling for sizing and autoscale (e.g., sustained for 5–30m windows)

3) Budget guidance: you referenced a target cost bucket per million tokens. If you can share a target $/1M (or range), that helps us pick the right model/quantization and propose a committed slab.

I've attached a quick pricing bands CSV and a draft mutual action plan to illustrate options (commit + burst carveout vs pure pay-as-you-go). If you prefer, we can sketch two scenarios: conservative (99M tokens/month, 200 TPS peak) and optimistic (120M tokens/month, 350 TPS peak) — tell me which is closer.

Next step: if you can reply with the three items above by EOD tomorrow, I'll run numbers and send a short proposal with a recommended band and expected $/1M.

Thanks —
Rishi

On Wed, Aug 19, 2025 at 3:12 PM Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Rohan / Ava — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can lock down a hosted pricing proposal: 

Thanks Rishi — good recap. Answers below (best-effort / working assumptions):

1) Monthly tokens: our pilot will generate ~20M tokens/month. If successful, we expect to roll out to 2–3 additional markets over 6 months. Steady-state after those expansions is roughly 80M tokens/month (we're budgeting conservatively at 75–90M).

2) TPS / QPS:
  - 99th-percentile peak TPS during marketing spikes: ~220 TPS (short windows, 2–3 minutes).
  - sustained QPS ceiling (5–30m windows): we expect sustained ceilings around 65 QPS (based on our internal traffic shaping). Note: our traffic model expects short bursts to 220 TPS but most windows sit under ~70 QPS.

3) Budget target: finance is looking for ~$12–16 per 1M tokens as a target range (we know we may need to trade off latency / model quality).

Question for you: how does Redwood treat short 99th spikes versus sustained QPS for billing and SLA? We have a small requirement for guaranteed trough-latency during spikes.

—Rohan

Thanks Rohan — that's really helpful. Quick notes and an initial pricing readout: 

- Got it on steady-state: 75–90M tokens/month. We'll model both 75M and 90M scenarios.
- Traffic shape confirmed: short 220 TPS spikes (2–3m), sustained ~65 QPS windows.
- Budget target $12–16 / 1M — noted.

Initial recommendation (hosted):
  - If you prioritize lower unit cost and can tolerate best-effort latency on spikes: commit slab at 75M tokens/month with a burst carveout for short spikes -> estimated list-equivalent $/1M ~ $11.5 (with a 12-month commit and limited burst buffer).
  - If you require tighter spike latency guarantees (99th SLO during bursts), we'd recommend a slightly higher slab or a dedicated reserved lane: list-equivalent $/1M ~ $14.5 with SLA-backed latency targets (adds capacity overhead).

I'll draft two short scenarios (numbers + expected latency tradeoffs) and attach. Also answering your question: for hosted we size for sustained windows and allow short burst buffering; billing is primarily token-based, but SLA-backed reserved lanes are priced to account for headroom needed to honor 99th spikes. I'll outline the math in the proposal.

Next step: I'll send the two scenarios by EOD today. Marissa, can you confirm whether we have runway to offer an introductory MAP at $13.5 / 1M for a first-year commit in this band?

Thanks —
Rishi
